input: The position on the outstanding order has deteriorated further, and the supplier delay affecting the package now stands at 4 weeks. The cause of the delay lies outside the supplier's own works: a breakdown at the foundry that casts the housings for the order brought casting to a halt, and without the castings the supplier has been quite unable to machine, assemble, or ship the outstanding units, leaving partly finished work standing idle in its shops in the meantime. Efforts are being made to recover at least part of the lost ground. The remaining castings are to be split between the foundry, once its repairs are complete, and the alternate supplier that is already qualified under the EPC arrangements, and this split should allow machining to restart on the first castings rather than waiting for the full quantity. The procurement manager owns the split and its day-to-day management, and will report progress against it to the project board until the backlog has been cleared.
target: The supplier delay on the outstanding order stands at 4 weeks, and its cause sits outside the supplier's own works. A breakdown at the foundry that casts the housings for the order stopped casting, and without castings the supplier cannot machine, assemble, or ship the outstanding units. The castings are on the critical path for the package. Machining cannot start without them, and assembly and shipment queue behind machining, so a stop at the foundry moves every later step in the sequence by the same amount and leaves partly finished work standing idle in the supplier's shops. Recovery rests on splitting the remaining castings. Part goes to the foundry once its repairs are complete, and part to the alternate supplier already qualified under the EPC arrangements, so machining restarts on the first castings back instead of waiting for the full quantity. The alternate supplier holds the same qualification for the housings and needs no fresh approval, which is what makes the split available at once rather than after a further round of assessment. The procurement manager owns the split, the expediting of both sources, and the revised delivery sequence, and reports progress against it to the project board until the backlog clears.
